operations.summary: Send one prompt to a catalogue model and get the reply back synchronously. The charge is metered on the prompt and reply token counts at the model's published prices and debited from your 2Z balance; the response says exactly what was charged. The most this request can be charged (the prompt plus the longest reply asked for, plus a reasoning allowance on models whose output limit does not cover their reasoning) is held from your balance before the model is called -- refused with 402 if you do not hold it -- and the difference is returned when the reply is priced. No transcript is kept: use the conversation endpoints for one. Send an Idempotency-Key to be able to retry a dropped connection and get the same reply back without paying twice; the reply is kept with that key for replay.

operations.summary: Charge the server-set price (GET /api/e2ee/chat-requests/price/) from the caller and credit it to the recipient, atomically, and notify the recipient with an ENCRYPTED_CHAT_REQUEST event whose content_url opens e2e2z's first-contact screen for the caller's handle (the caller gets a read ENCRYPTED_CHAT_REQUEST row of their own, with no link, as the record of the spend). No message is sent. The Idempotency-Key is bound to the recipient; a replay returns the original result with `replayed: true` and never charges twice. Completed results replay for 365 days. Refusals (402, 404, 409 price_changed, 422, 429, 503) charge nothing and release (or never take) the key. Rate limits, per sender: 10 per hour, 30 per 24 hours, and 3 per 24 hours to the same recipient.

operations.summary: Show whether the current balance covers the next renewals.

Purchase 30 days only when the creator's transaction-locked price equals expected_price. A new subscription renews at that ceiling; an existing subscription retains its current renewal ceiling, including zero after cancellation. This explicit route supports backend-first rollout; clients must not fall back to the legacy subscription POST after an ambiguous response. Completed results replay for 365 days. A key that already completed a legacy POST /api/tuzis/subscribe/{username}/ for the same creator is replayed here too (replayed: true, nothing charged) rather than claimed anew, so a client may move an outstanding purchase intent from that route to this one without paying twice. That replay is the ONE 200 on this route that expected_price does not constrain, and it cannot be: the legacy route binds no price and records none, so the amount it debited is not recoverable from its receipt. Read it as 'this key already bought this membership, on a route that charged whatever the price was then' -- nothing is charged now, and `balance` is the fan's real balance either way. The same applies to a receipt reached through X-Superseded-Idempotency-Key. That carry-over replay only happens while the membership it bought is still running: receipts are kept far longer than 30 days, so a receipt whose month has already ENDED is not replayed -- you are not subscribed and it would be false -- and is not charged under that key either. It is 409 `idempotency_mismatch` with `key_resolved: true`, and the month is bought by the next request, under the fresh key that answer tells you to mint. Every replay on this route is guarded that way, including the replay of a receipt recorded under this very key. One other 200 is unbound for the same kind of reason: if your key already completed a purchase HERE, of a membership you are STILL holding from this creator, a retry of it at a different expected_price replays that purchase (replayed: true, nothing charged) rather than refusing. That key bought the month you are holding, so reporting it is the honest answer, and telling you to mint a fresh one would buy a second month for a fan trying to recover one purchase. Retire the key on that 200 like any other, and a deliberate extra month is then a normal purchase at the current price. Once the membership has lapsed the same retry is a 409 `idempotency_mismatch` with `key_resolved: true`, because then the receipt really does describe a request that is over. A NEW debit is always bound to expected_price. expected_price 0 confirms a FREE membership (a free follow): it grants the same 30 days and moves no 2Z, so `charged: true` there means the membership was extended, not that 2Z moved. On every 200, `balance` is the fan's balance as of this reply, including a replay; `charged` and `expires` describe the original request.

operations.summary: Every language variant of this zPage with its real status. The source variant is first and carries `origin: "source"`; translations follow, sorted by tag. operations.summary: Update part of one language variant — publish a draft, fix a title — without resending the body. Owner only. A PATCH cannot *create* a variant: title and content are required for that, so use PUT. Publishing a 97th translation returns 409; existing published translations, drafts and unpublishes remain valid.

operations.summary: One language variant of a zPage. Unlike `GET /api/zpage/{id}/?lang=`, this does **not** fall back to the source variant: a language with no variant is a 404, so a client can use it to tell 'not translated yet' from 'translated'. A draft variant is visible to its owner only. The response carries this variant's strong `ETag`; send it back as `If-Match` to make a write to this variant conditional.

operations.summary: Create or replace one language variant. Owner only; a non-owner gets 404. Writing the page's own `source_language` updates the canonical article, so the source really is a variant like any other. Creating a variant requires `title` and `content`; send `If-None-Match: *` to create it only if nobody else has meanwhile (412 otherwise). Publishing a 97th translation returns 409; creating a 97th draft translation returns 409; edit an existing published translation, save a draft, or unpublish one instead.
